Photoreal procedural world — validation and roadmap

Reference Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21 Source: photoreal-world-roadmap.md

One seed, rule files (.nature, .mat, terrain and water graphs) and deterministic chunk streaming, so a whole photoreal world is generated on demand, always identical, and mostly baked. This page checks the idea against the code and lists what to build, in order.

1. Verdict#

Implementable, with the current stack (Rust/Iced editor, C++ engine on SDL3 GPU, C ABI). Nothing in the idea needs a new renderer. The hard parts are not graphics: they are determinism, chunk borders and connecting the generators. Most of the rendering features a "photoreal" pass asks for already exist; the missing piece is the world layer that connects terrain, nature, materials and water.

The idea has four parts. Their status in the repository:

Idea Status Evidence
Procedural materials, multi-frequency, anti-tiling Done, tune with recipes ~123 procedural ops, 78 presets, Variation class (material-pipeline.md)
Depth: parallax, micro-shadows, AO, IBL Done POM with self-shadow, geometric displacement, height-derived AO, env map + probe IBL (scene_lit.frag)
Rules as files (.nature, .mat, terrain/water graphs) Done per tool, not linked each generator saves its own graph and places assets
Seed → deterministic world, streamed by chunk Partial ProceduralStreamer + hash01(cx, cz, seed) exist, but use a built-in fbm terrain and props, not the generators
Vegetation/rocks adapted to terrain, scattered by masks Partial scatter core + biome table + Scene > Scatter on Terrain (C ABI v16) place plans by slope, wetness and height (terrain-generator-guide.md); streaming by chunk and the generators' output as scatter content are still open
Instancing, LOD, impostors for mass vegetation Partial instanced draws (also with painted vertex colour), wind, translucency and alpha-tested shadows exist; Micromesh cluster LOD now draws dense opaque parts (rocks, trunks) through the scene renderer (micromeshes.md); foliage cards still have no LOD chain or impostors

2. Review of the claims in the original discussion#

Kept as true, with caveats that matter for the design.

  • "Stable by derived seeds." True, and already how the streamer works (hash01(cx, cz, seed, salt)). Caveats: (1) use an integer hash (xxHash or SplitMix) per cell, never floating-point sums; (2) never let a parallel reduction decide the order of results, sort by cell id; (3) pin the noise and libm calls (or avoid sin/pow in anything that decides placement), otherwise two platforms place a tree a metre apart; (4) version the algorithm: a change to a .nature op changes every tree, so each rule file carries a generator_version and old worlds keep the old behaviour or are re-baked on purpose.
  • "Save only rule + position + sub-seed." True for generated content. Anything the user edits (sculpted terrain, a moved tree, a deleted rock) must be stored as a sparse delta layer over the generated world, or editing breaks determinism. Add this from the start.
  • "Generate once per chunk, freeze the result." Right, and it fixes the performance worry. Cache by (world_seed, chunk, rule hashes, generator_version), on disk as well as in RAM (this is the "pre-compiled" part of the idea).
  • Chunk borders are the real trap. A tree whose crown crosses a chunk edge must not be duplicated or cut. Use cell ownership: placement runs on a global jittered grid (or blue-noise/Poisson cells); a cell belongs to exactly one chunk, and a chunk generates its own cells plus a margin read-only to resolve collisions with neighbours' cells, using the same deterministic order.
  • "Trees do not cross rocks or each other." Solve it at placement, not at mesh time: priority classes (rocks, then trees, then bushes, then grass), exclusion radius per class, and a density mask. This is cheap and deterministic. Per-vertex raycasts are only for the trunk base.
  • Ground conforming. Sample terrain_height(x, z) (exists in the C ABI) and the terrain normal. Trees take a blend of up and the normal (small factor), rocks sink by the lowest height under their footprint, grass follows the normal. Root flare and rock skirts need a deformed base mesh and vertex colour (not done, see phase 3).
  • Contact blending. Correct: vertex colour on the base plus a ground blend in the shader. Needs the vertex colour channel that the Nature Generator does not have yet.
  • The pasted Height-to-AO code (Rust, 8 directions): the idea is right, and we already ship an AO from height. If it is reused: the parallel version has a typo, the direction (0, 2) should be (0, -1), and the slope term height_diff / distance ignores the world scale of the texel, so AO strength changes with resolution. Compare with ours before replacing anything.
  • "Photorealism is only the graph." Partly. Photoreal also depends on scale and variety: one bark texture on every trunk looks fake at any quality. Per-instance tint, wetness, wind and seasonal variation matter as much as extra noise octaves.

Corrections specific to this project:

  • The original text speaks of SDL_CreateTexture, a 2D API. The engine uses SDL3 GPU; mips are already generated (createMippedTexture, box filter). Better filtering (Kaiser) and an explicit anisotropic sampler setting are optional improvements, not a gap.
  • Normal blending (whiteout) already exists as a graph node; the preview material path does not need a new blend function.
  • Specular IBL here uses an equirectangular sky and a probe; a prefiltered cubemap with a BRDF LUT is the proper split-sum form and a possible quality upgrade, not a missing feature.

3. Target architecture#

text
world.cworld  (seed, generator_version, layer list, edit deltas)
   ├─ terrain graph  → height + masks (slope, wetness, flow, biome)   [exists: terrain generator]
   ├─ biome rules    → density per class from the masks               [new]
   ├─ scatter rules  → .nature / .rock / grass refs + placement rules [new]
   ├─ water graph    → water bodies from flow and sea level           [partial]
   └─ material layers→ splat/blend from the same masks                [partial]

per chunk (worker thread, deterministic):
   masks → placement (cells, priority, exclusion) → instances (transform + sub-seed + variant)
        → bake cache (RAM + disk) → GPU instance buffers per LOD → draw

Principles: (1) a chunk is a pure function of the world file and its coordinates; (2) generators produce data (fields, instance lists, meshes), the renderer never runs a graph; (3) only commands via Messages and MCP actions, as in the rest of Doppio; (4) libcaffeine-capi stays the only boundary.

4. Roadmap#

Each phase ends with something visible and testable headless. Do them in order; phases 1 and 2 are independent of renderer work.

Phase 0 — Determinism foundation#

  • [x] core/Hash.hpp: SplitMix64 deriveSeed(parent, salt, x, z), toUnit, GENERATOR_VERSION; golden test tests/test_hash.cpp pins outputs, recipe_ref.rs pins the same numbers in Rust.
  • [x] The streamer's placement decisions go through placementHash(version, ...): version 1 is the legacy hash01, version 2 the SplitMix64 of core/Hash.hpp. ProceduralWorldComponent::generatorVersion stores the choice and defaults to 1, so existing worlds do not move; new worlds should set Core::GENERATOR_VERSION. Tested in tests/test_scatter.cpp.
  • [x] generator_version field in every generator.* recipe (nature, material, texture, terrain, water).
  • [ ] The same field in bare .mat files and in the world file (there is no world file yet).
  • [x] Test: derived seeds for a block of cells are identical on 1 and on 7 threads (tests/test_hash.cpp).
  • [x] The same test for whole generated scatter chunks: 1 and 7 threads give identical results, and cutting the world into 32 m, 48 m or 96 m chunks gives the same instances (tests/test_scatter.cpp). Whole streamer chunks (cubes) still to do.

Phase 1 — Terrain masks exported to the engine#

  • [x] The terrain exposes named masks as engine-readable fields: height, slope and curvature derived by the engine from the heightfield (exact, nothing stored), and flow (D8 drainage), wetness, wear and deposit (erosion) sent by the generator as 8-bit masks, saved with the terrain file (version 3). The Output node gained optional Wear and Deposit inputs (the presets with erosion wire them). 8 bits is the one precision; 16-bit masks were dropped as unneeded for weights. Picture in terrain-generator-guide.md.
  • [x] C ABI v15: set_terrain_mask, terrain_mask_count/at, terrain_mask at a point, terrain_mask_rect over a rectangle, terrain_normal at a point (POD info struct); the Rust crate wraps them. Tested on both sides: tests/test_terrain_masks.cpp, tests/test_capi.cpp, and an engine-backed Doppio test that places the Alpine Range and checks every mask against the heights.
  • [x] Biome table (terrain/TerrainBiome): per scatter class, base x a product of trapezoid terms over masks, as plain text, plugged into the scatter module's density callback; an unknown mask places nothing and is listed by missingMasks. Tested with the scatter module (trees never on steep or wet ground, rocks only on the ridge). Not yet read or written by the editor: that is the World tab (phase 6).
  • [ ] Masks still to make: height bands as named masks (height covers the raw value; a band is a biome term today), a wear mask for terrains that did not use hydraulic erosion, and masks painted in the editor.

Phase 2 — Scatter engine (core, no UI)#

  • [x] scatter module (src/caffeine/scatter/Scatter.hpp): jittered grid per class, density from a callback (the biome maps will plug in there), exclusion radii, priority order, ownership by position and a margin for chunk borders. Conflicts use a non-recursive rule (a point yields to any closer point with a higher key, whether or not that one survives), so a chunk needs only a margin of two radii and never depends on its neighbours or on load order.
  • [x] Output: instance list (position, up, yaw, scale, variant, sub-seed, tint); conformed to height and normal with per-class rules (tiltToNormal, sink per scale, tint jitter, scale range). Rock sink by footprint minimum is still a single sample at the centre.
  • [x] Tests: no overlap inside and across chunk borders (all pairs over 3 x 3 chunks); same result for any chunking and load order; density follows the mask; priority classes are unaffected by lower ones.
  • [x] C ABI v16 and the Doppio Scatter action: scatterTerrain (region, chunk-size independent) behind caffeine_session_scatter_terrain and caffeine_biome_check; Scene > Scatter on Terrain and the agent action scatter_on_terrain place a text plan (Scatter/*.scatter) as entities in one undo step, with the biome table as density. Tested in tests/test_scatter.cpp, tests/test_capi.cpp and engine-backed in Doppio (terrain-generator-guide.md).

Phase 3 — Nature assets that can be scattered#

  • [x] Vertex colour and a painted flutter weight in the Nature mesh output: OBJ v x y z r g b a, read by the engine into a second vertex stream (no ABI change); wind sway, flutter and translucency are material fields (C ABI v9).
  • [x] Material slots per submesh: OBJ usemtl groups load as sub-meshes, the Mesh Filter's Material slots (a.mat;b.mat) give each its own authored material (one draw per slot, so shadows, alpha and Micromesh follow the slot), no ABI change; the Nature generator's Merge parts places a model as a solid and a cut-out entity with a slot per part. Tested in tests/test_material_slots.cpp and engine-backed in Doppio.
  • [ ] Base deformation: root flare and rock skirt from a ground height callback at bake time.
  • [x] Variants: N seeds per nature recipe baked into a cached variant set (recipe_ref::nature_variants, doppio-material variants).
  • [x] Per-instance tint and scale range (ScatterClass::tintJitter, minScale/maxScale). Applying the tint through the Mesh Renderer modifier (C ABI v10) is the missing last step of the scatter integration.
  • [ ] Ground-contact blend in the shader (rock/trunk to ground colour using vertex colour).

Phase 4 — Rendering at scale#

  • [ ] GPU-instanced vegetation with per-chunk instance buffers. The instanced path now also covers meshes with a painted colour stream (nature scatter parts are placed as batched copies); the 256-per-batch limit and per-chunk buffers remain.
  • [x] Cluster LOD for opaque parts (rocks, trunks, boulders): Mesh Renderer -> Micromesh draws a mesh as a GPU-selected cluster cut, crack-free, with shadow cascades, vertex colours and sub-meshes, and optional occlusion. Measured on 81 dense rocks and a 300-tree forest: 6.1x and 3.3x fewer triangles (micromeshes.md, ./scripts/benchmark-micromesh.sh).
  • [ ] LOD chain from the same graph for what Micromesh does not take (alpha-tested foliage cards, wind-animated parts): simplified cards and a billboard impostor atlas baked per variant, distance and screen-size switching with dithered cross-fade. Also open: the Nature generator now switches Micromesh on for solid parts of 3 000 triangles or more (the Nature Micromesh option); terrain and water do not.
  • [ ] Culling by chunk, then by instance, on the CPU first; GPU culling only if profiling asks for it. (Per-instance frustum culling exists and is counted in the frame stats; there are no chunks yet; Micromesh culls clusters on the GPU, with occlusion against last frame's depth, for the meshes that opt in.)
  • [x] Wind (vertex stage, also in the shadow pass), leaf translucency, a normal map on leaf cards and alpha-tested shadows for cut-out cards.

Phase 5 — Streaming and caching#

  • [ ] Chunk jobs on the engine thread pool with a priority queue and a per-frame time budget; never block the viewport (same rule as the generator bakes).
  • [ ] Persistent bake cache keyed by (seed, chunk, rule hashes, generator_version); invalidation when a rule file changes.
  • [ ] Edit layer: sparse deltas for sculpt, moved or removed instances; applied after generation.
  • [x] Engine side of bigger heightfields: the C ABI accepts terrains up to 4097 x 4097 and the chunked LOD draws them; a 1025 x 1025 terrain (2.1 M triangles) submits about 0.84 M in about 410 draws (benchmark set). Measured, not just allowed.
  • [ ] The terrain generator still outputs 129, 257 or 513 only, and there is no tiling or streaming of a terrain larger than one heightfield (the terrain guide still says 513 and lists a tiled or GPU path; its limit text predates the 1025 measurement).

Phase 6 — Editor integration#

  • [ ] A World tab: seed, layer list, biome table, rule files per class, region painting of overrides.
  • [ ] Place and preview a chunk grid in the viewport; show cache hits and chunk build time in the HUD.
  • [ ] UiId entries, undoable edits (App::commit), MCP actions and a headless flow for each step.
  • [ ] Docs: update the Nature, Terrain and Water guides and the website pages; regenerate captures through the headless driver.

Phase 7 — Visual quality pass (parallel track)#

  • [ ] Prefiltered environment cubemap + BRDF LUT (split-sum); keep the current path as fallback. (Today: the equirectangular sky with mips, per-object probes and an analytic split-sum approximation of the BRDF term in scene_lit.frag.)
  • [x] Run-time modifiers (C ABI v10): tint, wetness, snow, age on the Mesh Renderer and the material; scripts can drive them per entity. Driving them from terrain masks is open.
  • [x] Water on the GPU: Gerstner waves in the vertex shader (no per-frame mesh rebuild), ripple detail, depth colour and foam.
  • [x] Generated bark sets (oak, pine, birch) with parallax relief; grass and soil surfaces from the Rock Surface bake are still open.
  • [ ] Reference scenes with fixed seeds, rendered headless, used as visual regression baselines. (The benchmark set already generates its content by hashes, byte-identically, and its triangle and draw counts reproduce exactly, but nothing compares pictures against a stored baseline yet; the water-dark-patch and Micromesh scene tests compare two renders of one run.)

Where it stands (2026-11-20)#

22 items done, 17 open. The finished work is the foundation and the rendering side; what is missing is the world layer that connects the generators, which this page called the missing piece from the start.

Phase Done Open State
0 Determinism 5 1 complete for what exists (hash, versions, thread-count tests); the world file does not exist yet
1 Terrain masks 3 1 done (7 masks, C ABI v15, biome table); painted masks and bands open
2 Scatter engine 4 0 done: core, C ABI v16 and the Scatter action place plans by the terrain's masks
3 Scatterable nature 4 2 vertex colour, variants, tint/scale and material slots done; root flare and ground blend open
4 Rendering at scale 2 3 wind/translucency/shadows and Micromesh cluster LOD done; foliage LOD and impostors, chunk instance buffers open
5 Streaming and caching 1 4 engine accepts big terrains; no chunk jobs, no bake cache, no edit layer
6 Editor integration 0 4 not started (no World tab)
7 Visual quality 3 2 modifiers, GPU water, bark done; prefiltered cubemap and image baselines open

What is left, in the order that unblocks the most (each item ships alone):

  1. Phase 1, masks to the engine done: the scatter module's density callback, the run-time modifiers and the splat/material blend can now read masks.
  2. Phase 2, the Scatter action done: the finished scatter core, the biome table, the variants, the tint and the Micromesh/instanced draw paths now show up in a scene (Scene > Scatter on Terrain). Its limit is scale: every instance is an entity, which is what phase 4's per-chunk buffers fix.
  3. Phase 3, material slots per submesh done, with the Nature generator switching Micromesh on for dense solid parts. What is left of phase 3 is the base deformation (root flare, rock skirt) and the ground-contact blend in the shader; both want the terrain height at bake time, which the scatter action now has.
  4. Phase 4, foliage: simplified cards and a billboard impostor atlas, then per-chunk instance buffers and chunk culling.
  5. Phase 5: chunk jobs with a time budget, the bake cache, then the edit layer (design the delta format before the editor exists).
  6. Phase 6: the World tab, once 1 to 5 give it something to drive. Phase 7's image baselines can start now: a scatter scene exists to render (scripts/render-scatter-docs.sh).

The one decision that is not engineering: the world file (world.cworld) has no owner yet. Phases 0, 5 and 6 each need it; define its layers and delta format before phase 5.

5. Risks#

Risk Mitigation
Float differences change placement across machines integer hash, versioned algorithm, golden tests (phase 0)
Chunk-border duplicates or gaps cell ownership and read-only margin (phase 2)
Generation hitches while moving time-budgeted jobs, cache, prefetch ring (phase 5)
Many materials per tree break batching slots per submesh (done: one entity, one draw per slot, instanced batches keep working per slot), atlas variants, impostors (phases 3, 4)
User edits break determinism sparse delta layer from day one (phase 5)
Scope: seven generators in one world each phase ships alone and is useful without the next
